# Fenrir apps

Fenrir is one free, self-hosted codebase that runs either as the **complete** platform or as **one app on its own**.
Each app has its own dashboard showing only its pages, its own README and a full guide. Fork the repository, choose an
app during setup, and run it independently.

| App | `FENRIR_APP` | What it is | Device agents |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Fenrir (complete)](../README.md) | `complete` | Everything below in one console, joined up (alerts open tickets, devices feed compliance). | Yes |
| [Fenrir RMM](rmm/README.md) | `rmm` | Remote monitoring and management for the devices you look after. | Yes |
| [Fenrir Antivirus](av/README.md) | `av` | Endpoint protection: antivirus and EDR with a security operations console. | Yes |
| [Fenrir Vulnerability Manager](vuln/README.md) | `vuln` | Find, rank and fix vulnerabilities, and prove they are fixed. | Yes |
| [Fenrir CRM](crm/README.md) | `crm` | Customer relationship management for IT service businesses. | No |
| [Fenrir PSA](psa/README.md) | `psa` | Professional services automation: the service desk and the business behind it. | No |
| [Fenrir GRC](grc/README.md) | `grc` | Governance, risk and compliance programmes you can evidence. | No |
| [Fenrir Microsoft 365](m365/README.md) | `m365` | Microsoft 365 administration across all your customers' tenants. | No |
| [Fenrir Mobile](mobile/README.md) | `mobile` | Phone management: Android phones and web protection for Apple devices. | Yes |
| [Fenrir Docs & Vault](docs/README.md) | `docs` | IT documentation and an encrypted credential vault. | No |

## How it works

- `FENRIR_APP` in `deploy/.env` picks the app (setup writes it: `deploy/setup.sh --app rmm`).
- The server mounts only that app's API routes and runs only its background jobs; other apps' addresses answer
  404. `GET /api/app` says which app is running.
- The console reads `/api/app` and shows only that app's menu, pages and home dashboard.
- Every app includes the core: sign-in and two-step sign-in, customers, users and roles, settings, webhooks, API
  credentials, approvals and the audit log.
- Apps never depend on each other. Where one would hand work to another (a monitor opening a ticket, say), the
  hand-off happens only when both run on the same server; otherwise it is skipped and the app's own record stays.
- All apps share one database design, so you can switch an existing server to `complete` (or another app) later and
  keep your data.

The app definitions are in [`cloud/fenrir_cloud/apps.py`](../cloud/fenrir_cloud/apps.py) (server) and
[`console/src/appinfo.tsx`](../console/src/appinfo.tsx) (dashboard). These documents are generated by
[`apps/build_docs.py`](build_docs.py).
